newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, liquidation in RSS1 seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, liquidation in RSS1 seen.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market drifted quietly along by the midday break on Wednesday with some liquidation seen for RSS1 rubber as the trade looked for leads going into the afternoon session, dealers said.
Easier prices in Japan, where the key November contract shed 0.5 yen to 132.3, prompted local players to mark their prices lower in the morning, they said.

"It's still on a downtrend. The market is still very weak. There are a lot of sellers hoping to unload their material, but there were few takers so far although the afternoon should bring a different picture," a trader said.
"I think there was a dealer who liquidated their position in RSS1, but the tonnages involved were probably small," another dealer said.
The trade is looking for fresh incentives after largely lacklustre activity yesterday when only the October/December month of the TSR20 FOB contract saw moderate activity.
At 0430 GMT, August RSS3 was indicated at 110.00 U.S. cents a kg from 111.00 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 154.00-156.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08-$1.09) a kg from 158.00 cents.
